head: 0222c9b9af3c7347d90cb97bb383a74cd097b7a5
summary:
This is a stale re-validation of SL-075 on the merged tree, HEAD 0222c9b on top of the uat merge 77ed010.

**What the merge brought in.** Outside .taad/slices, the only change is .taad/fitness.yaml. SL-074 deleted its '# settled by SL-043' block, which removed three settled rules (-30 lines). src, tests, harness.py, divergences.json, eng/dotnet.ps1, global.json and RuleCases.ps1 are all unchanged since 6f49ae3. Build attempt 2 answered the merge by changing only eng/rules-harness/plants.json:
- The three deleted names are gone from `also_settled` on F20, F21 and F23.
- F23 keeps SL-044's 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends'.
- One `_note` sentence was rewritten.

**What I measured on the merged tree:**
- **The main run.** harness.py with --engine-root set to the taad_v3 backend (faecfc3, clean) and --scenario all, on this tree's own .dotnet (SDK 10.0.401):
  - The header names the engine root's fitness.py.
  - Parity is AGREE 11 <- 15, 27 patterns; 46 settled.
  - The clean baseline is 11 Facts and 61 rules, 0 hits, CLEAN.
  - Result: 52 rows, 52 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0, in 19 s. F20-F23 are each fire/fire.
  - git status was the same before and after.
- **Mutated copies, to check the rows can still fail** (a temp plants file outside the tree). All four were caught, exit 1:
  - M20 (F20 with the deleted settled twin put back) gave MISSED-BY-FITNESS. This confirms that SL-074's deletion really changed the engine's behaviour and that the committed row is the right one.
  - M21 (F21 relabelled '(App)') gave MISSED-BY-FITNESS and STRAY-HIT naming '(Core)'.
  - M22 (F22 recorded as fitness quiet) gave FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT.
  - M23 (F23 without `also_settled`) gave STRAY-HIT naming SL-044's rule.
- **RuleCases -Case All:** C-001 to C-014, 'All checks held.', exit 0, 402 s, git status unchanged.
- **rules-parity:** AGREE, exit 0.
- **Fitness tool:** 61 rules, all hold.
- **Row names:** every `also_settled` name in plants.json and divergences.json is a rule in the merged fitness.yaml (0 dangling, 0 duplicate rule names).
- **Anchors:** each still matches exactly one line: 22, 138, 523 and 52.
- **Missing --dotnet-from tree:** gives CANNOT MEASURE, exit 2.

Contact is 'code'. Everything here is the project's own harness, building a scratch copy and running xUnit plus a local checkout of the engine. For a slice that is only test data there is no device or live environment to reach.

**Declared departure.** The design's wording in criteria 1, 2, 5, 7 and 11 assumes F20, F21 and F23 list SL-043's settled twins. SL-074 deleted those twins, so the rows can no longer name them. Build attempt 2 and code review both declared this. The mechanism those criteria protect still holds: M20 and M23 show the harness rejects a row whose `also_settled` does not match what fires. I did not raise an obligation for it.

**Loop check.** This is not a loop. There were two build attempts: one original, and one caused by the merge's stale revoke, which fixed a real breakage the merge caused. No stage was sent back twice for the same cause.

**Housekeeping.** Two scratch folders my runs left (exit 1 and exit 2) are deleted, and my other runs cleaned up after themselves. %TEMP% holds 268 fsa-parity-case-* folders plus fsa-engine-case-*, fsa-rules-* and fsa-rules-case-* folders, all created between 20:31 and 20:54:15. That is before this session's tool host started at 20:54:30, so they are not mine. In total there are 1,948 fsa-parity-case-* folders in %TEMP%, a leak from earlier RuleCases runs. I left them in place.

criteria.criterion: 1. TheClassifierListsNoLinkTags fires on a hard-coded link tag (IO_REPARSE_TAG_SYMLINK const planted in EntryClassifier.cs, which also holds P07d and D3 plants)
criteria.how: On the merged tree, --scenario all gives F20 xunit fire/fire and fitness fire/fire, AS-RECORDED, with P07d quiet/quiet and D3 AS-RECORDED in the same run. F20 no longer names a settled twin because SL-074 deleted it. M20, with the twin put back, gives MISSED-BY-FITNESS, which confirms that twin is really gone.

criteria.criterion: 2. NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (Core) fires on `_store.VolumeUsedSource.Task.Wait();` in a Core file; the App entry stays silent
criteria.how: F21 is fire/fire AS-RECORDED with 0 stray hits, and judge() rejects any extra Fitness rule. M21, relabelled '(App)', gives 'did not fire (App)' and 'also fired (Core)'.

criteria.criterion: 3. NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure (App) fires on a blocking wait in the App project; the Core entry stays silent and the xUnit Fact fails
criteria.how: F22 is xunit fire/fire and fitness fire/fire, AS-RECORDED, with 0 stray hits. M22, recorded as fitness quiet, gives FIRED-WHEN-EXEMPT naming '(App)'.

criteria.criterion: 4. The two NothingWaitsOnTheVolumeFigure entries are told apart by the row's rule string
criteria.how: F21 and F22 ran in one batch and both came out AS-RECORDED. The yaml has them as separate entries (lines 198 and 206). M21 shows that swapping the suffix makes the row fail with MISSED-BY-FITNESS plus STRAY-HIT.

criteria.criterion: 5. TheVolumeReadHoldsNoScanStore fires on a ScanStore reference in VolumeSpace.cs; SL-044's settled rule also fires
criteria.how: F23 is fire/fire AS-RECORDED with also_settled set to SL-044's rule. M23, with no also_settled, gives STRAY-HIT naming 'Core does not publish a live ScanStore before the scan ends', so that rule does fire.

criteria.criterion: 6. Clean baseline stays quiet on the edited tree
criteria.how: The clean phase of every harness run on the merged tree: xunit 11 Facts, 0 hits | fitness 61 rules, 117 files, 0 hits, none unmatched, CLEAN. The one rule NOT RUN is the import rule, which needs a code graph that the scratch copy lacks.

criteria.criterion: 7. Committed rows reproduce the spike's outcomes and the old rows do not move (39 rows, --scenario all, divergences.json unchanged)
criteria.how: 52 rows, 52 AS-RECORDED, 0 stray hits, exit 0. The xunit and fitness expectations for F20-F23 equal the spike's fire/fire. divergences.json has no diff. As declared, the spike's extra settled-twin hits no longer exist after SL-074.

criteria.criterion: 8. The outcome comes from the TAAD engine at --engine-root, even with taad3.fitness importable elsewhere
criteria.how: Every run's header names C:\Users\sshub\projets\taad_v3\backend\taad3\fitness.py. RuleCases -Case All, which includes C-006's decoy-on-PYTHONPATH and preloaded-decoy checks, held with exit 0.

criteria.criterion: 9. RuleCases.ps1 agrees with the new row counts (no stale 35/19/F19 literal)
criteria.how: RuleCases.ps1 is unchanged since attempt 1, and that run's grep found no literal counting rows. -Case All holds C-001 to C-014 on the merged tree, exit 0. Reflect already noted that the criterion's premise was vacuous.
AGREE 11 facts <- 15 twinned entries, 27 patterns; 46 settled, exit 0. The drop in settled entries from 49 to 46 is SL-074's deletion, not this slice's.

criteria.criterion: 11. A row that omits a settled twin fails
criteria.how: M23, which omits SL-044's still-live settled rule, gives STRAY-HIT with exit 1. For X01 and X02 (F20 and F21) there is no settled twin left to omit after SL-074. M20 shows that naming the deleted twin fails as MISSED-BY-FITNESS, so the harness still insists that also_settled matches what actually fires. The design's wording assumed the twins exist; that is a departure already declared by build and code review.

criteria.criterion: 12. Evidence written into the tree before the run (an untracked, non-ignored .cs under .taad/slices/SL-075 copied into the scratch tree)
criteria.how: The slice folder holds only .json and .txt (15 files, no .cs). My run copied the untracked evidence into the scratch tree (600 files) and the baseline stayed CLEAN at 52/52. I did not plant a .cs to see what one would do; the design marks it material false.

criteria.criterion: 13. No .NET 10 SDK on this PC (--dotnet-from points at a missing tree, no network)
criteria.how: Re-run on the merged tree: --dotnet-from C:\nonexistent-sl075-tree gives 'CANNOT MEASURE ... has no eng/dotnet.ps1', exit 2, and records no outcome. The no-network download branch of eng/dotnet.ps1 was not exercised.

not_reached: No real device or live environment. The deliverable is test data for the rules harness, so the strongest contact available is the harness's scratch-copy dotnet build, the xUnit run and a local engine checkout. That is contact 'code'.
The engine measured is the taad_v3 checkout's backend at faecfc3, not a packaged TAAD engine, because none exists on this PC. Another engine revision could record different outcomes for F20-F23.

Fitness never reaches verdict 'pass' on the scratch copy. The import rule 'the provider does not use the code it checks' is NOT RUN for lack of a code graph, so F20-F23 are measured only on the must_not_match half and the xUnit twins.
The no-network branch of eng/dotnet.ps1 was not exercised. This tree already has SDK 10.0.401, and simulating a network loss would mean touching network settings.
No .cs file was planted under .taad/slices/SL-075 to see whether a *.cs Fitness glob would disturb the baseline. The design marks criterion 12 as material false.

F17-F23 are asserted only by plain harness plants/all runs. RuleCases C-008 is fixed at F01-F16, and nothing flags an also_settled name that no longer exists until the harness runs with the engine. SL-074's deletion showed both gaps. build-slice already raised both as open.

%TEMP% holds 1,948 fsa-parity-case-* folders, 268 of them created between 20:40 and 20:53 today, before this session. It looks like a RuleCases cleanup leak from earlier runs, since my own full run left none. This was not investigated further and is not attributable to this slice's diff.
